title: Drift-aware region arbitrator with asymmetric hysteresis and soft variant fallback
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem:
Customers intermittently see elevated tail latency or increased error rates when cross-region links degrade. Existing region selection uses simple percentile thresholds which oscillate during transient network spikes and does not gracefully fall back across model variants. This causes wasted retries, flapping between regions, and poor UX for SLA customers.

Goal:
Provide a production-safe region arbitration policy that: (1) detects sustained degradation (not single-sample noise), (2) prefers stable decisions (asymmetric hysteresis to avoid flip-flop), (3) can soft-fallback across model variants (full model -> quantized -> smaller model) with traffic shadowing + staged ramp, and (4) exposes tunable knobs per-customer SLA.

Design summary:
- Signals: p50 and p95 latency histograms, packet_loss (percent), retransmit_rate (TCP), rtt_jitter (ms), and infra error rate. Each signal is normalized to a 0..1 health score.
- Composite net-health score: weighted sum with default weights {p95:0.45, p50:0.15, packet_loss:0.2, retransmit_rate:0.1, jitter:0.1}. Scores are smoothed with an EWMA (alpha configurable per-signal) and combined into a rolling window of 60s/5m/30m granularities for short/medium/long-term views.
- Drift detection: sliding-quantile drift detector (ADWIN-like) on p95 and packet_loss with adaptive window resizing to distinguish gradual shift vs burst. Detects sustained shifts before triggering policy.
- Asymmetric hysteresis: separate thresholds for degrading and recovering transitions. Example: degrade threshold when net-health > 0.7 sustained for 90s; recover threshold when net-health < 0.45 sustained for 5m. This reduces flapping while allowing quick degrade detection for safety.
- Variant fallback policy: tier-aware fallback plan per region. For each region, we maintain compatible model variants ranked by resource cost and quality. Fallback sequence: primary-fullprecision -> quantized-8bit -> small-footprint model. Fallbacks are staged via soft-ramping: start with 5% shadowed traffic processed by fallback variant, evaluate quality (log-prob deltas and eval prompt set) and latency; if OK, gradually ramp at 2x per minute until 50% then monitor 30m stability before full switch.
- Safety gates: minimum sample count (N>=200 requests/min), max rollback rate, cooldown window after any fallback action, global circuit-breaker for runaway error increases.
- SLA precedence: customers with "priority":"enterprise" get lower degrade thresholds and conservative fallback sequences; free-tier may prefer cost-first variants.

Implementation notes:
- Telemetry pipeline: additional aggregation job to compute per-pop p50/p95 + packet_loss windows; stored in timeseries DB with 10s rollups.
- Runtime: region-arbiter service consumes composite scores and produces routing directives. Decisions are versioned and audited to console.
- Config API: per-customer policy objects stored in ConfigDB; rollout flags to enable experimental hysteresis params.

Observability & Telemetry:
- New dashboard: "Region Arbiter — NetHealth" with short/medium/long net-health lines, drift alerts, fallback actions timeline, per-variant quality delta charts.
- Alerting: page when any region has net-health > 0.85 for 5m or when fallback quality delta exceeds threshold.

Benchmarks (staging):
- Controlled link-loss injection: when packet_loss increased from 0.2% -> 2.5% sustained, composite net-health tripped degrade path at ~70s and soft-fallback completed 50% ramp in 4 minutes with p95 latency improvement of 28% on affected region.
- Recovery case: after link repaired, hysteresis prevented immediate revert; system recovered at ~7 minutes (configurable).

Open questions / trade-offs:
1) Weight tuning: weights above are conservative; need automated tuning per-customer class (follow-up ticket).
2) Quality validation: do we require golden eval set per-customer to approve a variant ramp? For now rely on sampling + generic prompt set.
3) Storage cost of longer telemetry retention vs sensitivity.

Acceptance criteria:
- Composite net-health computed and visible in staging dashboard.
- Drift detector signals correlated with synthetic degradations in canary tests.
- Asymmetric hysteresis params applied and prevent more than 1 flip per 15m in stability tests.
- Soft-fallback ramps successfully in staging with quality checkout and automatic rollback on failures.
- Config knobs available per-customer and documented.

Next steps / rollout plan:
1) Merge staging PR and run 4-day soak on non-critical tenants (canary group).
2) Collect metrics: flop-rate, p95 delta, fallback frequency.
3) Gradual rollout to enterprise tenants with lower thresholds.
4) Post-rollout: A/B test weight optimization and consider ML-based weighting.
